title: Eagles head coach Nick Sirianni says they are building more of a connection on this road trip for the joint practices and game in New England “These first two days obviously are all focused on practice and then we'll be focusing on getting ready for the game. But naturally, yeah, guys will go out to eat together. Guys will spend time together. Coaches will spend time together. Coaches and players will spend time together. There's a lot of time, too, where they're just together, being together. I think one thing we talk an awful lot about when we talk about connection is you can form connection through adversity of tough practices, of adversity that you face as a football team together. You can grow connection through building trust on a daily basis, but there is no substitute. You have to spend time. You can't just form a connection without spending time with each other. There is no shortcut on that. It's like, how do you gel a team quickly to come together? Time is one of the most important things that we have here on this to be able to build a connection as a football team. This is just probably a more carved out time than they get because they're not going back to the hotel or anything like that. You spend more time together in that. I always appreciate that about this portion of a joint practice.”

title: Some notes from Kevin Stefanski's presser up in Indy for the Falcons' second day of joint practices with the Colts: - On signing of Za'Darius Smith: Stefanski has a "comfort level" with the edge rusher, sees him as "a guy who can play on all downs." - Said he would like to see protection "clean up" ... a focus today is on getting protections in a better spot from a technical standpoint - Jake Matthews doing better, was held out a bit through Day 1 but still nothing concerning. Expects him back more today. - Expressed confidence in Jawaan Taylor and him upping how much he's in the mix with the first team. Taylor told media yesterday he underwent a clean-up knee surgery in March, which is why he's missed time to this point. - With starters not playing in Saturday's game, Cooper Rush and Jack Strand will split halves at QB
summary:
Some notes from Kevin Stefanski's presser up in Indy for the Falcons' second day of joint practices with the Colts: 
- On signing of Za'Darius Smith: Stefanski has a "comfort level" with the edge rusher, sees him as "a guy who can play on all downs."
- Said he would like to see protection "clean up" ... a focus today is on getting protections in a better spot from a technical standpoint 
- Jake Matthews doing better, was held out a bit through Day 1 but still nothing concerning. Expects him back more today. 
- Expressed confidence in Jawaan Taylor and him upping how much he's in the mix with the first team. Taylor told media yesterday he underwent a clean-up knee surgery in March, which is why he's missed time to this point. 
- With starters not playing in Saturday's game, Cooper Rush and Jack Strand will split halves at QB
full_text:
Some notes from Kevin Stefanski's presser up in Indy for the Falcons' second day of joint practices with the Colts: 
- On signing of Za'Darius Smith: Stefanski has a "comfort level" with the edge rusher, sees him as "a guy who can play on all downs."
- Said he would like to see protection "clean up" ... a focus today is on getting protections in a better spot from a technical standpoint 
- Jake Matthews doing better, was held out a bit through Day 1 but still nothing concerning. Expects him back more today. 
- Expressed confidence in Jawaan Taylor and him upping how much he's in the mix with the first team. Taylor told media yesterday he underwent a clean-up knee surgery in March, which is why he's missed time to this point. 
- With starters not playing in Saturday's game, Cooper Rush and Jack Strand will split halves at QB

title: Nick Sirianni will throw the challenge flag this year. Coaches are allowed to delegate the responsibility on the sideline for the first time. Here's why Sirianni will keep it: "We had a quick discussion about it, but yeah, I'm definitely going to keep that because my direct communication upstairs, again, I don't want to have a misstep or anything like that where -- There's times on the challenge flag from my perspective that-- "I think back to 2022, Smitty catches a ball over his shoulder at Washington. We run a play fast and (Ron) Rivera throws the flag, but the ball is being snapped as he throws the flag. We actually beat the challenge. In my eyes, the way we need to do it, the way the Philadelphia Eagles are going to do it, is I just want that direct communication so if I have to get the flag out quick -- I'm not saying my release is really quick. I'm not saying anything like that, but at least I can get that out quick. That's just my feeling on it of what we're going to do. I know sometimes it comes down to just little tenths of seconds to be able to get that flag out per the 2022 Washington game."

title: Jalen Hurts Training Camp Stats, Day 14/Day 2 vs Patriots: Jalen Hurts and the offense had an up-and-down day vs the Patriots The start to the day couldn’t have gone worse as Hurts first pass was intercepted. The pass was to Hollywood Brown in tight coverage and the result was the ball deflecting into the air and eventually intercepted Hurts followed that up two plays later with a touchdown to Dallas Goedert over the middle of the field from about 10 yards out. Goedert was wide open and Hurts hit him in stride. The rollercoaster day continued from there as Hurts threw his second interception. This time the pass was picked off in the front corner of the end zone as the corner jumped infront of Dontayvion Wicks and kept his feet inbounds. Like his first interception Hurts followed that up with a touchdown, this time finding Wicks in the back of the end zone on a similar play to his first touchdown. But on the biggest drill of the day Hurts came through With the ball 25 yards from the end zone Hurts hit Goedert and Wicks on back-to-back plays to get the ball to the five yard line. He followed that up by standing in the pocket, waiting for the play to develop and hitting Hollywood Brown for the practice-winning touchdown. He followed that up by hitting Darius Cooper for the two-point conversion. There is no question the offense struggled for a good portion of the day but scoring at the end to win the practice was a positive ending for Hurts Day 14 Stats: 9/15, 4 TD, 2 INT 2026 Stats: 166/241, 14 TD, 11 INT

Jalen Hurts Training Camp Stats, Day 14/Day 2 vs Patriots:

Jalen Hurts and the offense had an up-and-down day vs the Patriots 

The start to the day couldn’t have gone worse as Hurts first pass was intercepted. The pass was to Hollywood Brown in tight coverage and the result was the ball deflecting into the air and eventually intercepted 

Hurts followed that up two plays later with a touchdown to Dallas Goedert over the middle of the field from about 10 yards out. Goedert was wide open and Hurts hit him in stride.

The rollercoaster day continued from there as Hurts threw his second interception. This time the pass was picked off in the front corner of the end zone as the corner jumped infront of Dontayvion Wicks and kept his feet inbounds.

Like his first interception Hurts followed that up with a touchdown, this time finding Wicks in the back of the end zone on a similar play to his first touchdown. 

But on the biggest drill of the day Hurts came through

With the ball 25 yards from the end zone Hurts hit Goedert and Wicks on back-to-back plays to get the ball to the five yard line. He followed that up by standing in the pocket, waiting for the play to develop and hitting Hollywood Brown for the practice-winning touchdown. He followed that up by hitting Darius Cooper for the two-point conversion. 

There is no question the offense struggled for a good portion of the day but scoring at the end to win the practice was a positive ending for Hurts
